entities.summary: Racism is the belief that groups of humans possess different behavioral traits corresponding to inherited attributes and can be divided based on the superiority of one race or ethnicity over another. This ideology has its roots in ancient Greece, where philosophers such as Plato and Aristotle discussed the concept of races and their supposed superiority. The idea of racism was later perpetuated by European colonizers and slave traders, who used it to justify the enslavement and exploitation of people of color. In the 17th century, the concept of racism was formalized in Europe through the work of scientists such as Carolus Linnaeus, who categorized humans into different races based on their physical characteristics. The legacy of racism can be seen in the ongoing struggles of people of color against discrimination and oppression, as well as in the ways in which it has shaped modern society, from the distribution of wealth and power to the way people interact with one another. Racism has also had a profound impact on the way we think about ourselves and our place in the world, contributing to feelings of inferiority, shame, and anger among those who are marginalized. Despite its harmful effects, racism has also been a driving force behind social change, inspiring movements such as the Civil Rights Movement and the Black Lives Matter movement. As we move forward in the 21st century, it is essential that we confront the legacy of racism and work towards a more equitable and just society for all.
